Lina (sales): AsterBio needs a quick POC decision: VPC peering vs PrivateLink. They insist on forensic-quality client-ip evidence, a single IP to whitelist for their egress firewall, and the minimal ports to open. Can we give short paste-ready lines for procurement and a recommended option?

Gus (netops): Short answer: peering preserves network-layer client IP end-to-end. PrivateLink places connector ENIs in customer VPC so network source becomes ENI. For forensic-level netflow you want peering.

Ana (eng): If they choose PrivateLink but still need provenance we can add a signed header on HTTP: X-Redwood-Proof: base64(hmac)|ip|ts|reqid. Requires a verification key on their side. For non-HTTP TLS streams signed headers aren't possible; peering or an in-VPC proxy is required.

Tom (security): Signed header is acceptable for many audits but not a cryptographic proof of device identity. For chain-of-custody that maps back to network interfaces use peering + netflow export from their VPC. We'll provide suggested header format and key rotation guidance.

Gus (netops): Minimal firewall snippet to paste: outbound TCP 443 to our control plane CIDR (we'll provide exact CIDR at handshake); if PrivateLink allow inbound TCP 443 from connector ENI CIDRs; if peering allow 443 over peering and update routes. Allow UDP 123 to time source.

Lina (sales): Single egress IP — can we promise one IP they can whitelist?

Gus (netops): They can NAT connector egress through a NAT Gateway/Transit EIP in their account. That yields a single Elastic IP they control. We don't supply the EIP inside their VPC. With peering the original IP is preserved so they can control egress NAT at their border.

Ana (eng): Perf note for POC: for sustained high throughput pick peering + TGW + dedicated subnet to avoid MTU/ENI limits. PrivateLink is easier to set up but watch per-ENI bandwidth. For burst SLA we should propose a Dedicated capacity commit.

Tom (security): Paste-ready procurement lines: "Logs: request metadata and operational logs are retained per customer-configured retention in the Private deploy control plane; payloads are not retained unless customer enables audit logging. Keys: customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; Redwood integrates with cloud KMS or BYO HSM."

ticket-bot: Handshake ticket created: https://redwood.internal/handshakes/AB-1147 - netops to attach ENI CIDRs, sample SG, and signed-header docs.

Lina (sales): Thanks — I'll send peering recommendation for forensic needs, and include the signed-header option if they pick PrivateLink. Please upload the CIDRs and the header sample by EOD so I can lock the kickoff. :thumbsup:
